insight.title: You Are Closer to the Romans Than They Were to the Pyramids
insight.subtitle: How our brains flatten thousands of years of human history.
insight.notificationHook: You are closer to Rome than Rome was to Egypt

sections.text: We lump all of ancient history into one single, distant era. But Roman tourists visited the Great Pyramids and viewed them as ancient ruins, just like we view the Colosseum today.
The pyramids were already thousands of years old when Rome was founded. The gap of time between those two civilizations is wider than the gap between Julius Caesar and your breakfast this morning.
Our brains compress the deep past because we only see it in textbooks. We treat history like a flat painting, forgetting that the ancients had their own ancient history to marvel at.
Caesar studied ancient Egypt the same way you study Caesar.
